current_metrics.index_family_caveat: Linker leg's inflation_index_family is not surfaced by the breakeven primitive's current public wire — the basis primitive cannot directly verify whether the linker bond references the same inflation index as the ZCIS leg ('UK_RPI').  This basis is NOT a clean liquidity-premium read regardless: it also reflects index-lag differences between the ZCIS convention and the linker's realised CPI accrual, linker on-the-run / liquidity premium effects, AND structural ZCIS basis present even in benign markets.
current_metrics.methodology_label:
Swap-breakeven basis subtracts a generic linker-implied
breakeven from the corresponding ZCIS rate at the same tenor.
The result is NOT a clean liquidity-premium read: it also
reflects index-lag differences between ZCIS conventions and
the linker's realised CPI accrual, linker on-the-run /
liquidity effects, and any structural ZCIS basis that exists
even in benign markets.

Formula
-------
Per-trade-date,

  basis_pct = zcis_pct - breakeven_pct
  basis_bps = basis_pct * 100

where ``zcis_pct`` is the ZCIS rate level at ``tenor`` on
``zcis_curve_family`` (computed by
``calculate_inflation_swap_rate_level`` filtered by
``instrument_type='inflation_swap'`` AND
``pricing_type='zero_coupon_breakeven'`` AND
``curve_family=?`` AND ``tenor=?`` — the no-proxy guard
inherited transitively) and ``breakeven_pct`` is the generic
bond-implied breakeven for the same-tenor, same-currency
``(nominal_curve_family, linker_curve_family)`` pair (computed
by ``calculate_breakeven_inflation_simple`` which itself
composes a sovereign nominal yield_level with a linker
real_yield_level under their own four-conjunct discriminators,
plus the same-country invariant).

Composition path
----------------
The basis primitive composes two inner calls (the ZCIS
rate-level and the breakeven primitive) and inherits BOTH
sets of structural guards transitively.  The basis-spread
layer itself issues NO raw market-data SELECTs — every read
flows through one of the inner primitives.

Per-trade-date alignment uses a strict pandas inner-join on
calendar trade_date AFTER each leg's canonical TimeSeries is
produced; the basis is computed only on dates where BOTH legs
exist (no synthetic basis points are produced).  The inner
primitives' clean steps already apply ffill within
``ffill_limit_days``; the basis layer never adds its own
ffill across the inner-join.

Sign convention
---------------
basis = zcis - breakeven.  Per the catalog's
methodology_guardrails ("Must use the canonical sign
convention ZCIS minus breakeven", "Must not silently invert
the sign"), the convention is wire-locked at
``zcis_minus_breakeven``.  The compute layer raises
NotImplementedError if any other value is requested and
points the caller at methodology.planned_extensions.

Same-currency invariant (V1)
----------------------------
The basis is a same-currency object in V1 (e.g. USD_ZCIS with
UST/USD_TIPS, EUR_ZCIS with FR_OAT/EUR_FR_LINKER,
GBP_ZCIS with UK_GILT/GBP_LINKER).  The per-leg same-country
invariant on the breakeven leg (nominal/linker share country
+ currency) is enforced inside the breakeven primitive and
inherited transitively here.  The cross-currency basis
(USD_ZCIS minus EUR linker breakeven) is documented in
planned_extensions but not exposed as a knob — it would be a
separate primitive shape.

Index-family caveat
-------------------
Even within a single currency, the ZCIS leg and the linker
leg can reference different inflation indices in principle
(e.g. CPI-U non-seasonally adjusted vs CPI-U seasonally
adjusted; HICP vs HICP-xT).  ``current_metrics`` surfaces the
ZCIS leg's ``inflation_index_family`` / ``index_lag`` /
``interpolation`` / ``underlying_index`` and the linker leg's
metadata (whatever the breakeven primitive currently exposes
on its public surface) so the desk reader can decompose the
basis under the correct conventions.  The derived
``index_families_match`` flag and ``index_family_caveat`` are
surfaced top-level so the caveat is visible from one field.

NOT a clean liquidity-premium read — also reflects index-lag differences, linker on-the-run / liquidity effects, and structural ZCIS basis.
